apps.name: Buddy
apps.subtitle: Ask anything from the Dynamic Island
apps.localizedDescription: Buddy lives in your Dynamic Island. Tap it to ask, or double-tap the back of your iPhone to send a screenshot - the answer appears right in the island while you stay in your app. Free brain, no account.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Windows: your other AI agents now show up as pointers. When Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode works on your PC, Buddy shows each agent and each sub-agent as its own pointer, with its own name and colour and a bubble that says what it is doing: "explorer: Reading README.md". There is nothing to set up.
• The pointers wait in a column at the right side of the screen and fly to the window an agent's file is open in. A pointer hops at every new step, says "done" when its agent finishes, and leaves by itself. After 10 seconds without news only the name stays. At most 8 are shown.
• A bubble only shows the name of a file and the name of a program. Command lines, search words and file contents are never shown. Buddy only reads the agents' own history files on your PC; it sends nothing anywhere and never tells an agent what to do.
• Any other tool can join: Buddy.exe --crew "name: what it is doing", then --crew "name: done". Names, colours and icons can be fixed with crewlooks in the settings file (README, "Crew").
• Hand a question to an agent: type @opencode ..., @claude ... or @codex ... in the ask box (tap Ctrl+Alt+Space). Buddy opens that agent's own window with your words typed in, and the agent uses the model you set there.
• Buddy's own speech bubble is drawn once instead of on every frame, so a bubble on screen costs much less CPU.
• How it was checked: 335 automatic tests; on one PC with up to six live OpenCode sessions at once, in the built app. Three resting pointers cost about 1 % of one CPU core.
• Known limits: Claude Code and Codex are tested against recorded samples of their files, not against a live session, so they may show less than OpenCode does. @claude and @codex were not tried on a PC that has them. When several agents have the same name they are numbered, and the numbers can change as agents come and go (the colours stay).
